text: I've been using Microsoft Office in all its different versions since it first appeared.  I knocked two stars off because, among other things, Outlook 2016 doesn't have a unified Inbox.  Each email address has it's own .pst.  So, if you have multiple email accounts, you'll either need to look through multiple inboxes for your mail, or write a rule to direct all your accounts into a new .pst you'll create.  I did this, but that's not without its problems, too.  Unbelievable.  I like POP email because it resides on my local machine, and can be easily searched.  It's obvious Microsoft, in this version, wants you to use IMAP, which does no more than show you a picture of what's already in your web based email accounts.  The argument is that IMAP allows you to check email from multiple devices, but with POP you can still leave email on the server by simply checking a box (Gmail, etc).  And, IMAP makes searching for a key word among all your emails impossible.  I like the 5 machine licenses, but would rather have Outlook 2007 than this.  The forums are filled with complaints about Outlook 2016, and thus far, Microsoft is unresponsive.
title: If You Liked Outlook Before, You Might Not Like The 2016 Version

text:
I want to believe in a world in which redemption is always possible. There should be no unforgivable sins; your better qualities should always offer the hope that your failings, however profound, can be overcome.

But this shaver fails in the single unforgivable way that an electronic device can: despite lots of bells and whistles, it doesn't do the one thing you purchase it to do.

I bought this to replace an older model Norelco wet/dry shaver that finally gave up the ghost. This razor offers some additional features my old one lacked: it's much lighter, holds a charge longer, and has a silly and totally unnecessary shave-goo-dispensing system built into it. I tried to find a wet/dry Norelco shaver with no "moisturizing system," but to no avail. If you want to shave in the shower, Norelco wants to insure you keep purchasing more shave gel cartridges. After reading some reviews that suggested the shaver worked perfectly well without it squirting glop everywhere, I was satisfied this was the right purchase.

Unfortunately, the shaver is unsatisfactory in one way: it just doesn't shave very well. I've used it on my face and head, with and without moisturizer, wet and dry, and its shave is pretty lousy. My old Norelco provided a shave that was very smooth and comparable to a blade; with this model, there's noticeable beard fuzz left behind immediately after I shave, and by the end of the day, I look like I forgot to shave at all that morning. When I found myself going back over my face with a regular razor right after I used the 8040X, I knew this shaver had to go. I would like to believe that its lightweight, comfortable form and good battery life could redeem it, but sadly, its transgression is too profound. I may not be able to forgive it, but I'm pretty sure I'll forget I ever owned it before long.
title: Just can't do its job

text:
I am in LOVE with the DSi XL. The larger screen helps your eyes, the ability to listen to music is incredible and the Brainage titles are actually really, really fun!

This particular XL version is also very nice. The color is great, a nice Mario red that you don't get tired of seeing. The front cover has several cute Mario mushrooms and baddies on it. The two camera's make for some fun editing and time wasting but really aren't all that great as far as quality goes. But hey... it works.

The DS browser isn't all that great... it looks great, it works great but the internal memory only allows you to download two pages before the thing wonks out and makes you restart (the browser, not the DSi) after deleting cookies.

A great feature is the ability to turn off wifi in the settings menu. I love having control of that.

As for the game, if you do not already have Mario Kart than this is a great deal for you. The game is a full version and it comes with the case inside of the package. Not just the game card. If you already DO have the game than use this second one as a game card for your friends or family to play the full version with you. Its a win-win situation.

All in all, if you're looking for a DS to buy I would highly suggest this baby. For a mere ten bucks more than the plain versions you get a game and a beautiful cover. Its awesome.

text:
We ordered 2 of these harnesses for a new puppy we were getting, a small to fit it initially and a medium for when it outgrew the small.

The small was fine. It fit well and was secure. It stayed appropriately fit as we would go on walks or as the dog would play.

The medium was a different story. We would attach the belly strap at one length and whenever we would go for a walk the strap would continually loosen until it was as loose as it could be. It appears the material of construction for this strap lacks sufficient friction to hold it in place. I noted that this strap was indeed a different material than what is used on the small harness.

When I contacted the seller about this defect they told me it might get better if the dog gets bigger. Not terribly reassuring as the dog is a mixed breed and we have no idea if she will get any bigger.

They suggested I try to share it with someone else and offered me $4 in a refund.

Terrible customer service. I do not recommend this company or brand. There are many other products out there. Try one of those.

text:
I've owned this marvelous machine for one year now.

Here's what I love:
♡ It has never leaked, the water pump works flawlessly draining and preventing over-filling during use. Win.
♡ It's very quiet. If the clothes aren't distributed evenly in the drum during the spin cycle, it'll bang around, but there's a quick fix to stop it
♡ Gets out more dirt using less force; much gentler on clothes compared to many other washers I've used.
♡ Requires a ridiculously small amount of soap, even for very dirty, full loads. I usually shake the bottle of detergent, and just use what coats the inside of the cap.
♡ Still going strong, despite me purposefully putting it through its paces (over filling, sometimes running 10+ loads in a day, etc)
♡ It still works like it's brand new... sure, this is like repeating the previous point, but I'm compelled to say it again anyway :)

Dislikes:
⊗ The lint trap doesn't trap a dang thing in my machine. I resorted to using a metal sieve/strainer placed under the drain hose. It catches a ridiculous amount of lint and keeps it out of the pipes/drain
⊗ I wish the lid latched instead of just flipping open or closed. Because it just rests in the closed position, it tends to rattle during the spin cycle. Not all the time, small annoyance from time to time.
⊗ The water hookup hose that came with it has a non-standard thread cap, and I was unable to find a way to hook it up to my water line. I just use the handheld shower hose to fill it up. A trip to home depot would probably solve this though, so no biggie, just me :-P

I bought a rolling cart for it to sit on for mobility, making it easier to store.

I definitely recommend this machine if it fits your price range. It's a workhorse! I'm happy I bought it :)
title: I've owned this marvelous machine for one year now...

text:
I just bought Madden 12 for PS2 a week or so ago. It is very similar to Madden 10 (I bought 11 for WII, did not enjoy).

very smooth game play (upgrade to madden 10)

The bad:

I spent the first 2 hours just updating as many rosters as I could think of-barely made a dent overall.

The worst:
Commentating. By far the worst commentating of all Madden games (I've been playing since 01 version). Collinsworth has almost the exact same lines from Madden 10, and his commentating sucks overall-but the other guy's is even worse. You can really tell that parts are attached together (AND HE BREAKS AWAY!!!! (sigh), for the touchdown....). Just horrible, horrible, horrible commentating overall.

I really like Madden games overall, but I just feel like the producers don't really give a crap anymore. I'd like to see some other NFL games emerge and make the Madden producers try again- even minor upgrades would be awesome. Get other guys to comment, and make them say more than 5 or 6 phrases.

text:
We have gone through at least five Ice Maker Machines of this size, trying to find a model that doesn't have "issues" of one kind or another. This Euhomy machine has finally met our desires and expectations! Great operation, bigger bullet cubes than others, and has a self-cleaning function as well.

The build of this machine is well-designed and robustly engineered. After letting it sit for an hour to settle, filling the water tub and turning the ice maker on produced the first ice cubes in 6-minutes...and continued every 6-7 minutes afterwards.

The machine has two ice size settings and the large ones are better, larger, and clearer than any of the machines we have previously used. The noise level is low and unobtrusive, and the top indicators are clear and intuitive.

The machine has a self-cleaning function which works VERY well and used regularly, will keep the machine in top condition and providing clean and safe ice.

The machine senses low water and will stop automatically. It will do the same for overflow of ice and resume operation automatically when the overflow either melts back down into the water container or is cleared manually. Simple, yet highly effective operation and controls.

I am so pleased to have FINALLY found a countertop ice maker that works without issues and provides great ice while having the self-cleaning features of this one. It is great in our kitchen for bullet ice cubes and travels with us in our RV when on the road.

It's an unequivocal FIVE STAR rating for me, and earns my honest and hearty recommendation. Best we have used and sold at a very fair price on Amazon. Superb!

(Update 8/5/17)
I am not able to make more comments on the quality of the replacement violin, because unfortunately they don't have a violin in their inventory to send me a replacement. I received a refund instead.

I would like to repeat that I am very pleased with the customer service. They do pay attention to the customer's concerns. If I were to rate the service itself, I would give 5 stars. As this is mainly a product review, I decided to give it 3 stars overall.

(Update 8/2/17)
The seller representative contacted me and offered a replacement. Very good customer service so far. I will update the product review after I receive the replacement violin.

(Original review on 7/15/17, 2 stars)
The violin looks pretty, and once we managed to get it tuned, gives ok sound, considering its price. There are several problems, though. First, it's difficult to tune it and keep it tuned. The tuning knobs do not stay in place - they pop loose easily. Second, the G string keeps sliding off the bridge (I see another reviewer also has this problem). Third, the strings are too close to the finger board near the top (due to the ridge on the top end of the fingerboard being too low). The result of that is, when a finger presses down on a string, a longer portion of the string makes contact with the finger board than needed to, and the sound is off. This effect is most pronounced when playing pizzicato (plucking the string), when instead of a tone from clear string vibration, you hear some buzzing sound and off key. A violin repair guy told me that the finger board is also slightly curved upwards, which is not a good sign.
Overall a good looking piece with accessories, but quality is not enough for serous playing and learning.
title: Gives ok sound, but with several serious problems... Good customer service.

text:
I tried switching from TurboTax Premier to H&R Block Deluxe this year. It was able to import data from our TurboTax return from last year, but it was not able to import most of our financial data from investment accounts that (at least last year) TurboTax had no trouble with. The system for valuing donated items seemed easier to use that TT's. But the real showstopper for me was a missing form. While Block has the form for claiming the tax credit for an electric vehicle, it is missing the form 8911 for the tax credit for an electric vehicle charging station. I would guess that at least 60% of people who buy or lease an electric vehicle are going to install a charging station, so this omission is rather silly. I can fill out the form manually and patch it rather awkwardly into the return, but this means that I cannot e-file with this software this year. I will likely go back to TurboTax next year, and I may have to re-do my taxes in TT this year, just to make sure that things that require continuity (e.g., IRA info) are kept up-to-date properly.

The other problem with the Block software is the difficulty in contacting their support people. This can only be done by phone or via Twitter. I got good responses via Twitter, but there are a lot of things that require more than 128 characters to explain. The two times I called, I used up 25 and 50 cellphone minutes, respectively, just waiting in their queue. They should have a way of contacting support people via email, or at least have the sort of queue where you can leave a phone number and have them call you back.
title: H&R Block deficient in forms and support access

text:
- I used this in a Keurig B40 (see pic) and there was a gap between the pod and the Keurig pod holder because of the two indentations at the top of the holder (see pic). Water was able to leak through that gap leading to a less than satisfactory brew and a bit of a mess as the water was able to flow outside of the holder. This holder is pretty standard for all the B and K series Keurings so I assume they will all have the same issue. I made a simple modifications to seal off that gap by putting a small rubber band (like the produce bands from the grocery store) around the top. It still fit in the holder and it didnt leak (see pics).

- the filter screen of the pod worked really well with minimal sediment even with a fine grind. I have ordered some paper filter inserts and will see if that works even better, but even without them this was more than acceptable. I have used some other reusable cups that use a mesh screen, and those let a lot of sediment through. This was much better.

Bottom line is, if you are planning on using this with a B or K series machine with the cup holder that has the indentations, then you are going to want to modify it a bit to keep it from leaking. When it does work though, it works pretty well.

I'm going to test it with some different grounds to see how they taste. My first attempts led to weaker coffee than I wanted.

text:
Some of you may not be familiar with Red Dragon. They may not be as well known as Razer, SteelSeries, HyperX, ASUS, etc. but that doesn’t change the fact they are a major player in the PC accessories industry.

You can use the board wired (type C), 2.4 GHz wireless with included dongle or Bluetooth. The battery life on a full charge for me with full RGB going is usually 35-38 hours for me give or take. Longer with RGB off.

There is so much more about the board it would take me another 12 paragraphs to describe. Just go get this board. The 60% form factor and hot swappable abilities of this board, warrant a closer look at least.

text:
If you need a super low budget gaming headset, look no further. I haven’t had a headset for gaming because I just didn’t feel like spending the money for something I’d barely use, as I’m at best a casual gamer, but I got covid and was stuck home for a few weeks so I decided to pull the trigger. Of course, I refused to pay 20 bucks or more, so I did my amazon homework and stumbled upon these black n orange bad boys for $14.99. I was skeptical at first because it just seemed too good to be true. These didn’t have many reviews yet, despite having a 5 star rating and other headsets at the same price either seemed inferior in quality/build or had mixed reviews.

I took the gamble figuring I’d just return them if any issues, but have been so far, surprisingly impressed. For a barebones entry-level headset, this one checks off all the boxes.

Besides the standard features, the design and build is solid and not janky at all. The padding in the ears is very comfortable and breathable. I’ve played for hours with minimal if any ear fatigue. The stereo effect works perfectly and a couple of friends have confirmed that they can hear me clearly when I speak through the mic. I’m not sure if the sound quality is a solid 5 seeing as how I haven’t tried anything “better”, but for what I’ve used them for I couldn’t be happier. The noise cancellation is almost too good. This LG/Kenmore refrigerator filter is made of three layers glued into a white frame that fits into the refrigerator filter holder without a problem. The first layer is black filter fabric. The middle layer is a nonwoven matt of (presumably) carbon infused fibers. The third layer is light black foam with large holes. The purpose of the filter paper and the foam layers is to contain the fibers inside the filter. The entire unit is disposable so there is no reason to have the filter media come out of the frame so gluing the unit together is a good choice.

I compared this filter to the original filter and found that the original also had a layer of nonwoven black fibers sandwiched between a layer of white filter cloth on each side. This filter was 'welded' at the edges into a pillow that was removable from the frame and provided more resistance to air flow.

Time will tell if this filter does the job. I just cleaned out the refrigerator so its relatively odorless. This filter has the required ingredients to do the job, so I am hoping that my fridge stays smelling sweet and fresh.
title: Three layer air filter with a sturdy frame for LG and Kenmore

I bought this pop filter several years ago and for a while it was fine. It connected easily to my microphone stand's cylindrical rod and I could place it reasonably well.

But it became apparent that the major weakness was the connection between the clamp and the long flexible arm. Each item worked well, and it clamps to the square tubes on my latest microphone stand, as well as being able to adjust with the flexible arm. But where the flexible arm connects to the clamp is the weak point.

The arm connects with a simple screw joint, and it is easy to loosen that joint. The arm then sags and is impossible to get into the correct position. In order to have the joint screwed up enough to hold the arm in place, even when the joint is placed horizontally, you end up with reaction forces in the flexible arm that make it very difficult to position the filter correctly. I seem to be only able to hold the filter in place from above, otherwise the joint and arm move the filter away from the microphone.

Unfortunate, as it seems to work well apart from this design flaw.

I thought I'd try out this new pheromone to see how well it works compared to others I've used. So far, I've just been using two or three drops a day for five days and then two days off. 4.) More openess

There may very well be many other effects I don't know about. It's just a matter of experimenting and logging the results.

text:
The only time I’ve used a Switch has been playing on one that my friends own. Just these experiences has really intrigued me into getting my very own Switch. I love playing video games and I own an Xbox and PS4, so I figure at some point it was time to complete the trifecta. While I’m more of an Xbox person, I will say I am very impressed by the Switch. It is a very simple console, but genius in of itself. I’ve had some Nintendo gaming devices here and there. A SNES back in the day, but mostly their portable ones from the Gameboy to the Advanced to the DS and 3DS. The Switch combines that of a home console and a portable gaming device and for that I love it. I can put it in the dock and play it on my TV. I can play it handheld which will be great for road trips or maybe just wanting to play anywhere. This was a brilliant move by Nintendo and it makes the Switch really stand on its own.

Now what I’d say my favorite thing about the console is it’s simplicity. This device is made for one thing only and that is for playing video games. The console is both modern and old school at the same time. Would definitely recommend to anyone who really likes Nintendo and their games.
title: One of the Coolest Gaming Devices I’ve Owned

text:
I thoroughly enjoy playing Harry Potter videogames. Order of the Phoenix and Half-Blood Prince for PS3 are especially good, in that they really bring the stories to life and make you feel as though you're part of the action, especially in the way that they designed the map to be continuous. I love pretty much all the HP games that I've played so far - EXCEPT for this game and Order of the Phoenix for DS. Both games are SO poorly designed that they leave the player wondering if the designers were in a hurry, just plain not interested, or some pathetic combination of both.

One of the BIGGEST flaws of this game is the fact that the characters never move their lips when they talk. I HATE it when designers do that! >:-( I mean, are they SO lazy or in too much of a hurry to take the extra time needed to make the characters' lips move? And do they ACTUALLY think that we won't NOTICE that, like all of a sudden our favorite characters are VENTRILOQUISTS now?! Come ON! >:-(

Another problem is that there are no voice-overs or even MUSIC in this game. Just sound effects, silence, and subtitles. Are they trying to relive the "silent movie" era by putting that into videogames now or something?

Besides those ANNOYING design flaws and poor graphics, the game itself is pretty boring, which makes it even worse.

All I can say is, the designers had BETTER do a better job with Part II, because Part I SUCKS!!! >:-(

text: I have a Panasonic TV with a single TOS optical output. It goes into a receiver and we have external speakers. For several years now I've had to read subtitles because my hearing is so bad. I got a streamer to stream sound into my hearing aids but it was very expensive and didn't work that great. I got a TOS link splitter on Amazon and this device. I ran the TV optical output into the splitter and ran 2 TOS cables - one into the receiver and one into the Sound Processor. I ran a 15 foot cable so I can put the device next to my chair because it has a great volume control. The sound is really fantastic. It's powered by USB so be sure you have an adapter that lets you plug a USB cable into the wall so you can put it near you. This is the first time in years that I can actually hear dialog on movies. This is a very inexpensive (especially if you buy a used DSS, which I did) and simple solution to a horrible problem. I considered added a bluetooth transmitter to the system to get rid of the long TOSlink cable but it seems from what I've read that this introduces a delay. There is absolutely no delay now. If you have this problem I hope this helps you out because it's great for me!
title: hearing impaired solution for TV with optical sound output

The Laloirelle Deep Hydration Face Oil is a combination of many herbal ingredients and oils which are beneficial for skin moisturizing and rejuvenating. I bought this to replace a Schubb capo that I lost, and honestly wasn't terribly fond of. I figured I'd give the Amazon a shot because I've had generally very good luck with Amazon Basics products in the past, and I'm not at all a gear snob.

text: The pros do outweigh the cons with this litter but, the con is a huge one. This stuff tracks everywhere! I can sweep three times a day and it still gets tracked into all the rooms in a 1500 sq. ft. house. When I shook out a towel from one of the cat beds, at least (and I'm not exaggerating here) a quarter cup of litter fell out of it - and that was just one day's accumulation. On the other hand, it is very nice not to have to lug around a 40 lb container of regular litter. It  clumps better than the regular kind and the wet litter is much easier to scoop out of the pan - it doesn't stick to the bottom so badly. The cats seem to like it - at least no one has refused to go in the box like they have with other brands I have tried. Daily scooping is easy and the Glade scent really does take care of odors. I just wish they could do something about the tracking problem. I have gone back to the regular Tidy Cat with Glade because I am tired of constantly sweeping and still finding litter all over the house. I agree with another reviewer that if you have a garage room or somewhere to isolate the box from the rest of the house, the tracking problem would be outweighed by the good attributes of this litter. Unfortunately, I don't have that luxury, so the litter spreads everywhere. Bottom line: if the lightweight is all that is available and I desperately need litter, I would buy it again. Otherwise, I'm sticking to the original heavy stuff.
title: Clumps Great But Tracks Everywhere

text:
343 was able to find the perfect balance between giving us a classic competitive Halo experience with modern FPS mechanics. What results is probably the best FPS of the year in the multiplayer side of things.

Now the campaign is ok. Sure it got overhyped but it wasn't as bad as people I felt made it out to be. All it is is just a set up for Halo 6. The game literally parallels with how Halo 2 was. I just felt that 3 Master Chief levels was lame. However, Locke is not a bad character just a tad generic.

Now I see people whining about micro transactions. This is one of the few times I am ok with them. They are only for warzone and don't really give a player an advantage if you buy them. Plus it takes probably 4 or so warzone assault matches to get enough points for a gold pack. The micro transactions are OPTIONAL. Also some of the money made from them is going into the Halo tournament prize pool which I think is really cool for 343 to do that and the money also made from the micro transactions makes them more comfortable to not charge us for map packs. Also no spit screen blows, but I am at a point in my life when I play split screen once in a blue moon and play with my friends online. Not a big loss for me.

All in all, Halo 5 is just a great game. It has been a blast and I can't wait to see how 343 shapes it up over the year. Big Team Battle was just added and it is a blast. Looking forward to forge. Hopefully they can get the map rotation issue fixed. Enjoy!
title: A Blend of Old and New Gives us the Best Halo Game since Halo 3

text: There is absolutely nothing i dislike about this headset! I've been using them for about 5 or 6 hours a day for the last month and they fit perfectly, are super comfortable, and get the job done. Not a problem with the HyperX - because it has a separate control box for audio controls. Noise cancellation is on the HyperX is also fantastic, so all you hear is the game, music or even phone call that you're plugged in listening to. Cord length is generous and after a month of heavy use there's no sign yet of any wear & tear so no need to even think about using the spare pair of ear pads that came in the box. As any gamer will tell you, wearing a headset makes a huge difference because you can hear subtle sounds that you'd never hear no matter how high you had speaker volume cranked up, and this HyperX will not disappoint especially when its so reasonable priced. I highly recommend them and will soon purchase another pair in a different color for my son who somehow manages to go through other branded headsets every few months. text:
Nuance got it right with Dragon 4. I have used Dragon on my PC for more than 12 years and had been one of its greatest boosters. The initial release of Dragon 3 for Mountain Lion was quirky, but Nuance improved it with subsequent upgrades.

I have installed version 4 (4.0.2). 4.0.2 works great with the latest upgraded version of new Pages. I never tried Word on my Mac. I am a great fan of WordPerfect which I use on my PC. This comment was dictated with Dragon 4. I think the major problem was the initial release of version 3 was that it was released very shortly after the initial release of Mountain Lion. Apple subsequently released interim upgrades for Mountain Lion & Nuance eventually caught up with it.

Nuance did not release version 4 until almost 6 months after Mavericks was released. There were subsequent upgrades of Mavericks which eliminated some of its quirks. For version 4, Nuance waited until they could get it right.

l have used Dragon for more than 12 years on my PC and other software made by Nuance. The initial release of Dragon 3 for Mac was quirky on Mountain Lion but Nuance improved it with upgrades for that version. Version 4 was apparently designed to work with Mavericks and it works very well for me.
